title: Trading Policy

tiers.name: Designated Person
tiers.description: Directors; any person with authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the Company's activities (including the Company Secretary, CFO and their direct reports); any person who becomes aware of Inside Information through access to confidential material; and their spouse, children under 18, family trusts and family-controlled companies (deemed Designated Persons).

tiers.name: employees, consultants or contractors (other than a Designated Person)
tiers.description: Employees, consultants and contractors who are not Designated Persons; may Deal at any time provided they do not hold Inside Information, without the Black-out Period, approval or notification regime that applies to Designated Persons.

tiers.name: Chair
tiers.description: The Chair of the Company; a Designated Person whose own Dealing requires prior approval of the Board (rather than the Chair's own approval), and who acts as Approval Officer for other Designated Persons' Disposal Consent applications.

definitions.hedging_definition: any other transaction in financial products which operate to limit (in any way) the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to the release of the Company's quarterly results
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after the release of the Company's quarterly results

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to the release of the Company's half-year results
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after the release of the Company's half-year results

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to the release of the Company's full-year results
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after the release of the Company's full-year results

windows.start_anchor: 14 calendar days before the Annual General Meeting
windows.end_anchor: the date of the Annual General Meeting (inclusive)

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Chair, in consultation with the Company Secretary, may determine any other period to be a Black-out Period from time to time; the Policy does not address whether such additional periods are kept confidential.

rules.detail: Blanket ban on using Derivatives (which include options, forwards, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars, and any instrument limiting economic risk) over unvested equity instruments, including performance share rights.
rules.evidence: The Company prohibits the use of Derivatives in relation to unvested equity instruments, including performance share rights, and vested Company Securities that are subject to disposal restrictions (such as a 'Holding Lock').

rules.detail: Same blanket ban extends to vested Company Securities that remain subject to disposal restrictions such as a Holding Lock.
rules.evidence: The Company prohibits the use of Derivatives in relation to unvested equity instruments, including performance share rights, and vested Company Securities that are subject to disposal restrictions (such as a 'Holding Lock').

rules.detail: Derivatives may be used over vested positions free of disposal restrictions, subject to compliance with the law and the rest of the Policy, including prior written Chair/Board approval, outside Black-out Periods and post-dealing notification.
rules.evidence: Derivatives may be used in relation to vested positions which are not subject to disposal restrictions subject to compliance with the law and the other provisions of this Policy.

rules.detail: 'Hedging' is not a defined term, but the Derivatives definition's second limb ('any other transaction in financial products which operate to limit (in any way) the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities') is the operative hedging concept, and is banned over unvested equity instruments.
rules.evidence: any other transaction in financial products which operate to limit (in any way) the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities

rules.detail: The same economic-risk-limiting instruments are banned over vested Company Securities subject to disposal restrictions such as a Holding Lock.
rules.evidence: The Company prohibits the use of Derivatives in relation to unvested equity instruments, including performance share rights, and vested Company Securities that are subject to disposal restrictions (such as a 'Holding Lock').

rules.detail: Economic-risk-limiting arrangements may be used over vested, unrestricted positions subject to the ordinary law and approval/notification/Black-out requirements.
rules.evidence: Derivatives may be used in relation to vested positions which are not subject to disposal restrictions subject to compliance with the law and the other provisions of this Policy.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a forward-sale or similar structure that limits the economic risk of holding unvested securities falls within the Derivatives definition's economic-risk limb and is banned.
rules.evidence: any other transaction in financial products which operate to limit (in any way) the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities

rules.detail: A prepaid forward or similar monetisation over vested, unrestricted shares is an agreement to dispose of securities (Dealing) and/or a risk-limiting Derivative, both permitted subject to prior Chair/Board approval, notification and Black-out compliance.
rules.evidence: entering into an agreement to apply for, acquire or dispose of, securities

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy, despite the Policy otherwise expressly addressing derivatives and margin loans in detail.
Securities lending is not named anywhere and is not included in the Dealing definition.
CFDs are not named but are a derivative within the meaning of s761D of the Corporations Act, expressly referenced in the Derivatives definition, and so are banned over unvested equity instruments.
rules.evidence: derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars)

rules.detail: A CFD over vested, unrestricted shares is permitted subject to law and the Policy's ordinary approval/notification/Black-out requirements.
rules.evidence: Derivatives may be used in relation to vested positions which are not subject to disposal restrictions subject to compliance with the law and the other provisions of this Policy.

rules.detail: Absolute, unconditional ban on Designated Persons entering a Margin Loan (or similar funding arrangement) to acquire Company Securities, with no vesting-state distinction, no clearance route and no listed exception.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons may not: (a) enter into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities; or (b) use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.

rules.tier: employees, consultants or contractors (other than a Designated Person)
rules.detail: Clause 6.3 is expressed to bind only 'Designated Persons'; no equivalent restriction is stated for other employees, consultants or contractors.

Using Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement is expressly and absolutely prohibited for Designated Persons, with no vesting-state carve-out and no clearance route.
rules.evidence: use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement

rules.detail: 'Margin Loan' is broadly defined as 'any lending or similar arrangement allowing a person to borrow money to invest in securities using existing investments as security', so any secured financing against Company Securities (not just a conventional margin loan) is banned outright for Designated Persons.
rules.evidence: Margin Loan means any lending or similar arrangement allowing a person to borrow money to invest in securities using existing investments as security.

rules.detail: No minimum holding period or short-term dealing restriction is stated; the only timing constraint is the Black-out Period regime.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: 5 business days of the Dealing occurring
clearance.evidence: Any Designated Person (other than the Chair) wishing to Deal in Company Securities must obtain the prior written approval of the Chair or the Board before doing so. ... any Designated Person who Deals in Company Securities must notify the Company Secretary in writing of the details of the transaction within five business days of the Dealing occurring.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: 5 business days of the Dealing occurring
clearance.evidence: If the Chair wishes to Deal in Company Securities, the Chair must obtain the prior approval of the Board before doing so.

clearance.post_trade_to: Board (Approval Officer notifies the Board of any Disposal Consent granted)
clearance.evidence: In exceptional circumstances a Designated Person may seek written approval from the Chair (Approval Officer) to dispose of or transfer (but not acquire or otherwise Deal with) Company Securities during a Black-out Period (Disposal Consent).

exceptions.evidence: transfer Company Securities already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Designated Person is a beneficiary

invest in, or trade in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in Company Securities) where the assets of the fund or scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party
undertake to accept, or accept, a takeover offer

participate in an offer or invitation made to all or most security holders, including a rights issue, equal access buy-back, security purchase plan or dividend or distribution reinvestment plan, where the timing and structure of the offer or invitation has been approved by the Board

exercise (but not Deal with the securities following exercise) an option or right under an employee incentive scheme where the final date for the exercise of the option or right falls during a Black-out Period

acquire (but not Deal with the securities following acquisition) Company shares by conversion of financial instruments giving rights to conversion to shares (eg. options or convertible securities) where the final date for the conversion of the security falls during a Black-out Period
acquire Company securities under a bonus issue made to all holders of securities of the same class
acquire Company securities under a dividend reinvestment, or top-up plan that is available to all holders of securities of the same class
acquire, or agree to acquire or exercise options under a Company employee share plan
withdraw ordinary shares in the Company held on behalf of the Designated Person in an employee share plan where the withdrawal is permitted by the rules of that plan
acquire ordinary shares in the Company as a result of the exercise of options held under an employee share scheme

where the Designated Person is a trustee, trade in the securities of the Company by that trust, provided the Designated Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a Black-out Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Designated Person
the Designated Person is in severe financial hardship and a pressing financial commitment cannot be satisfied otherwise than by disposing of Company Securities

the Designated Person is required by a court order, or there are court enforceability undertakings, to transfer or dispose of Company Securities or there is some other overriding legal regulatory requirement for them to do so

exemption_authority: Limited to the Chair's (as Approval Officer) power to grant Disposal Consent in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship or court order/overriding legal requirement) under clause 4.2, which permits disposal or transfer only (not acquisition or other dealing) and only while the Designated Person holds no Inside Information. The margin loan / secured financing prohibition in clause 6.3 has no exemption route at all.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives include: (a) derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars); and (b) any other transaction in financial products which operate to limit (in any way) the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Policy expressly names 'collars' as an example of a regulated Derivative, confirming that a bank-structured collar is squarely caught by clause 6.2's vesting-based prohibition/permission regime rather than needing to rely on a general dealing-definition sweep.

bespoke_clauses.topic: absolute margin loan / secured financing ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons may not: (a) enter into a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any Company Securities; or (b) use Company Securities as security for a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar (borrowing against, or pledging, the collared shares) is an outright prohibition for Designated Persons with no clearance path, no listed exception and no vesting-state carve-out, which independently defeats the funded structure even where the derivative legs would otherwise be permitted on vested, unrestricted shares.

bespoke_clauses.topic: derivatives permitted on vested unrestricted shares
bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives may be used in relation to vested positions which are not subject to disposal restrictions subject to compliance with the law and the other provisions of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An unfunded collar (put and call without a secured loan) could be entered on vested shares free of a Holding Lock, subject to prior Chair/Board approval, timing outside Black-out Periods, and post-dealing notification to the Company Secretary.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Buy or sell orders for Company Securities which are placed but not completed outside of a Black-out Period are subject to the following restrictions once the Black-out Period commences: the order must be completed within five trading days otherwise it will lapse; and the order cannot be varied.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If collar orders are placed but not completed before a Black-out Period commences, they must complete within five trading days or lapse and cannot be varied, creating execution risk for multi-leg trades straddling a blackout.

bespoke_clauses.clause: In exceptional circumstances a Designated Person may seek written approval from the Chair (Approval Officer) to dispose of or transfer (but not acquire or otherwise Deal with) Company Securities during a Black-out Period (Disposal Consent).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even in hardship or court-order circumstances, the Chair may only consent to a disposal or transfer, not an acquisition or other dealing, so it cannot be used to authorise entry into a collar or a secured loan during a Black-out Period.

summary: A funded collar is not available to a Designated Person under this policy: clause 6.3 absolutely prohibits Designated Persons from entering a Margin Loan or similar funding arrangement, or from using Company Securities as security for one, with no clearance path, no exception and no vesting-state carve-out, which blocks the loan leg outright. The derivative legs are separately regulated by clause 6.2, which bans any Derivative (a defined term that expressly includes collars and any instrument limiting economic risk) over unvested equity or vested shares subject to a Holding Lock, but permits Derivatives over vested, unrestricted shares subject to the general law, prior written Chair or Board approval, timing outside the quarterly/half-year/full-year and AGM Black-out Periods, and notification to the Company Secretary within five business days. In other words, an unfunded collar (put and call only, no secured loan) could in principle be cleared on vested, unrestricted shares, but adding a loan secured on those shares is an unconditional breach for any Designated Person. There is no exemption authority that could rescue the financing leg, since the only discretionary relief (Disposal Consent for hardship or court order) permits disposal or transfer alone, not acquisition or other dealing. Ordinary employees who are not Designated Persons are not bound by the clause 6.3 prohibition, but they would rarely be the bank's target counterparty for this kind of facility.
